sections.h2: Which Huntington office bills my property tax?
sections.html:
Two town offices split the work. The Assessor values the more than 72,500 parcels in the town and its incorporated villages, and the Receiver of Taxes sends the bills and takes the money. The Town Board appoints the Assessor, while the Receiver is elected.

The Receiver's office is in Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street, Huntington, NY 11743, and the receiver listed on the town site is Jillian Guthman, Esq. Her office collects for the town, Suffolk County, the school districts and other taxing districts, and it also takes Dix Hills Water District payments. The town's page says the office does not set the rate or the assessment. It carries out collection under the New York Real Property Tax Law and the Suffolk County Tax Act. The office number is 631-351-3217.

Counter hours for payments are 9 am to 4 pm, Monday through Friday. The general office stays open from 8 am to 5:30 pm.

sections.h2: When are Huntington property taxes due?
sections.html:
Huntington sends one bill a year, in the second week of December. For the 2026/27 year the first half is due January 10, 2027 and the second half May 31, 2027. A due date on a weekend slides forward, and Town Hall lists extended payment hours until 7 pm on June 1, 2027. January 10, 2027 itself falls on a Sunday.

Two groups get extra days on the second half. Owners receiving Basic STAR have until June 4, 2027. So do seniors on the Senior Low-Income exemption or Enhanced STAR, though after June 1 they can only pay by mail or at the counter.

Because of a federal postmark change effective December 24, 2025, a mailbox drop may not receive a same-day postmark. The town says only a hand stamp at a post office counter is guaranteed, and the tax office cannot waive penalties for a payment that is neither postmarked nor received on time. Safer routes are paying online, calling the payment line at (877) 690-3729 with jurisdiction code 2012 and your 8 digit bill number, paying at Town Hall, or using the locked black box at Town Hall. Online payments carry third-party fees.

sections.h2: What does a late first-half payment cost in Huntington?
sections.html:
Interest on the first half starts at 1% on January 11 and climbs one point each month until it reaches 5% in the last three weeks of May.

Source: Town of Huntington, Interest and Penalty Calculation.

After May 31 the town can no longer take the money. Payment, with a 5% penalty and monthly interest of 1% counted from February 1, goes to the Suffolk County Comptroller, 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901, phone (631) 852-3000.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Huntington assessment?
sections.html:
File a written complaint with the Town Assessor's Office by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May. In 2027 that falls on May 18. The Assessor's Office is in Room 100 of Town Hall, and the number is (631) 351-3226.

  • March 1 is the taxable status date, and property is valued as of its condition that day.
  • May 1 is when the tentative roll is set and opened for public inspection.
  • Complaint forms and a fact sheet are available after April 1, and the town accepts only an originally signed copy. Faxed or emailed forms are rejected.
  • If the Board of Assessment Review denies the complaint, a court challenge follows. New York State lists a $30 fee for Small Claims Assessment Review, with a filing window of 30 days from the final roll.

Suffolk County boards meet on the third Tuesday in May, which is earlier than the fourth Tuesday used in most of the state. A seller who waits for the later date will miss the Huntington window.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply to Huntington homes?
sections.html:
The Assessor's Office handles every exemption, and applications are due by March 1 to count on the following December's bill. The town's FAQ lists these programs:

  • Senior Citizens Limited-Income, for owners aged 65 or older. The income ceiling is $58,400 for both town and county, with documented medical costs deductible.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income, with the same March 1 filing date.
  • Veterans exemptions: Alternative, Cold War, Eligible Funds and Gold Star Parent.
  • Home Improvement, which phases in the added assessment from a renovation over nine years, up to 400 in assessment.

Basic and Enhanced STAR are state programs. For questions, call the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance at 518-457-2036.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Huntington property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property, so the closing needs a current figure. The Receiver's office keeps the tax rolls, including changes of ownership and a list of taxes in arrears. Ask the office, before a contract is signed, which half of the current bill is paid.

If the 2026/27 bill is still open when you list, plan around two dates. Before May 31, 2027 the Receiver takes the payment. After that date the tax, penalty and interest must go to the county comptroller in Riverhead, and the amount keeps growing by 1% a month. Ask the title company to carry that payoff on the closing statement, using the figure the Receiver or the comptroller gives you in writing.

Dix Hills Water District payments also go through the Receiver's office, so a Dix Hills seller should ask whether a water district balance sits beside the tax bill. A buyer paying cash can close on a short timeline and settle the tax at the table. That is useful for owners in Huntington Station, Dix Hills or Greenlawn whose bills have fallen behind and who want the matter closed without waiting on a listing.

sections.h2: What is the Huntington housing market like?
sections.html:
Huntington sits on the North Shore of Long Island, with Long Island Sound to the north and Nassau County to the west. It was founded in 1653, and the arrival of the Long Island Rail Road in 1867 turned a farming and shipping town into a commuter base. The town covers 94.0 square miles of land. Its four incorporated villages are Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport, and hamlets include Dix Hills, Melville, Commack, Greenlawn and Huntington Station.

Census QuickFacts counts 205,891 residents in July 2025 and 71,542 households. About 88.7% of homes are owner-occupied, valued at $715,600 at the median. Household income reaches $168,029, median rent is $2,358, and workers spend 35.2 minutes getting to work on average. Major employers named in the town's 2025 budget include Canon, the Northport VA Medical Center and Huntington Hospital.

School districts named for the town's communities include Cold Spring Harbor, Elwood, Half Hollow Hills, Harborfields, Huntington, South Huntington and Northport-East Northport,.

faqs.q: When is the second half of Huntington property tax due in 2027?
faqs.a: May 31, 2027 is the listed date, with extended hours on June 1, 2027. Owners on Basic STAR, the Senior Low-Income exemption or Enhanced STAR have until June 4, 2027.

faqs.q: Where do I pay late Huntington property tax after May 31?
faqs.a: Send it to the Suffolk County Comptroller at 330 Center Drive, Riverhead, NY 11901. The comptroller's number is (631) 852-3000, and the amount includes a 5% penalty plus monthly interest.

faqs.q: What is Grievance Day in Huntington?
faqs.a: Grievance Day lands on the third Tuesday of May, so May 18 in 2027. The Assessor's Office must receive an originally signed complaint on or before that day, and fax or email copies are rejected.

faqs.q: How do I apply for a senior exemption in Huntington?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor's Office at (631) 351-3226 to join the mailing list, and file the application with proof of income by March 1. The income limit is $58,400.

faqs.q: Does the Huntington Receiver of Taxes set my tax rate?
faqs.a: No. The office collects and distributes tax. The town's own page says it does not determine the rate or the assessment.
